thread.title: Matt Bevin dropped many of his out-of state properties in 2017. Here's what else he owns

author: Louisville Courier Journal
title: Matt Bevin dropped many of his out-of state properties in 2017. Here's what else he owns
text: Activate your digital access. Matt Bevin dropped many of his out-of state properties in 2017. Here's what else he owns Tom Loftus , Louisville Courier Journal Published 11:32 a.m. ET May 1, 2018 | Updated 1:55 p.m. ET May 1, 2018 CLOSE Gov. Matt Bevin's house in Anchorage, Kentucky, has been controversial. Here's why. Rachel Aretakis, Louisville Courier Journal Buy Photo Gov. Matt Bevin in April 2018 (Photo: Michael Clevenger/Louisville Courier Journal) Buy Photo CONNECT 1 COMMENT EMAIL MORE FRANKFORT, Ky. — Gov. Matt Bevin appears to have sold considerable real estate holdings in 2017, according to the annual personal financial disclosure statement he filed late Monday. In the report, filed with the Executive Branch Ethics Commission, Bevin lists having a financial interest in only three properties — two houses in Louisville and one in Bryant Pond, Maine. But a year ago, and in three previous reports he filed with the commission, Bevin had listed holding an interest in 10 other properties — all but one of them outside Kentucky. Bevin's disclosure of having an interest in two houses in Louisville apparently reflects his controversial purchase in March of 2017 of a mansion in Anchorage. A year ago Bevin reported having just one house in Louisville. But the new report filed by the governor does not list anywhere his affiliation with Anchorage Place LLC, which is the company that purchased the Anchorage mansion. The latest: Bevin's home now valued at almost twice what he paid in controversial deal The governor's communications office did not immediately return a phone call and an email from Courier Journal on Tuesday morning. The governor is just one of more than 1,400 officials of the executive branch of state government required to file an annual disclosure report with the ethics commission. The reports were due April 16 covering the calendar year 2017. Bevin requested a two-week extension in filing his report, and he filed it electronically with the commission Monday night. The annual reports require only general information about the personal finances of a state official, but they provide the only information available from Bevin, who — unlike his recent predecessors as governor — has declined to release his income tax returns. The absence of these 10 properties is the biggest difference between the personal financial disclosure report Bevin filed Monday and the one he filed a year ago. No longer listed in the new report filed by Bevin are five single-family residential rental properties: one each in Louisville; Woodstock, Maine; and Leesville, Louisiana; and two in East Hampton, Connecticut. Also no longer listed in Bevin's recent report are timberlands that Bevin previously reported owning in Hampton, New York, and Claremont, New Hampshire, as well as commercial properties in East Hampton, Connecticut; Bethel, Maine; and Biddeford, Maine. Read this: What's Bevin hiding upstairs at his Anchorage mansion? Or in the barn? Last spring Courier Journal reported that Bevin and his family had moved into a mansion in Anchorage that had been purchased for $1.6 million by Anchorage Place LLC, a company whose owners are not listed in filings with the Kentucky secretary of state. The transaction became controversial because the sales price was very low compared to values that were placed on the mansion by the Jefferson County property valuation administrator and because the seller was a company owned by Neil Ramsey, a large donor to Bevin political causes who was appointed by Bevin to the board of the Kentucky Retirement Systems. Bevin initially declined to discuss the transaction but later acknowledged that he had purchased the property. But Anchorage Place LLC is not listed in the governor's new disclosure report. Bevin's companies Under the category for listing positions he or his wife holds "in a business, partnership or corporation" Bevin lists these four companies he also listed in his report a year ago: Integrity Holdings LLC, Bryant Pond, Maine, investment holding company, sole owner Golden Rule Signs LLC, Louisville, LED sign company, partner Neuronetrix Solutions LLC, Louisville, medical device company, board member Bevin Bros. Manufacturing Company, East Hampton, Connecticut, bell company, president Under the category of businesses in which he or his wife own an interest of at least $10,000 or that equals at least 5 percent of the business, Bevin listed these five companies that he also listed a year ago: Heart and Soul Candies, Louisville, candy company Integrity Holdings LLC, Bryant Pond, ME. Investment holding company Golden Rule Signs LLC, Middletown, LED signs Neuronetrix Solutions , Louisville, medical device company Waycross Partners LLC, Louisville, investment management company Another difference in this new report filed by Bevin is that in prior years he listed no other sources of income other than the companies he owned part or was affiliated with. This year in that category he reported "Stock Dividends in publicly traded securities: AAPL, COP, Etc." Bevin also reported that he remains president and board chair of Brittiney's Wish Inc., of Louisville, a charity he founded in honor of his daughter who died in a car crash. Like in recent years, Bevin's recent report says he has no creditors to whom he owes more than $10,000. And, as he did last year, the only gifts he reported receiving during the year worth more than $200 were University of Kentucky football and basketball season tickets and tickets to Keeneland's fall and spring meets.
